Kiln billing safeguards

See how AI work will be billed and deliberately approve detected API or provider billing.

01 / SECTION

Read Claude billing without extra friction

The account area explains the reported billing route. The decision beside these screens covers incomplete billing details.

Key acceptance criteria & mockups

  • A subscription account continues normally. Known paid overflow has a factual amber notice and a link to Claude usage settings, with no extra approval. Missing overflow information is never reported as disabled. AC-BILL-02–03
  • The subscription email appears directly below the subscription label. Existing usage gauges, including Weekly · Fable, remain visible independently of billing details. AC-BILL-07–08
  • A real sign-in or readiness failure still needs its stated remedy; an approval checkbox cannot bypass it. AC-BILL-02

What should work or look differently in this section?

Assumptions to confirm

BILLING-002Confidence: 90%Determines whether missing billing details can prevent otherwise ready work.Unanswered

Should a working sign-in continue when additional billing details are unavailable?

If authentication readiness passes and Kiln detects no API/provider override, unavailable additional billing metadata does not prevent Start or automatic recovery. Show a neutral Claude Code settings summary, with optional details, and require no acknowledgement.

A detected override still requires approval even when other fields are missing or conflict with a subscription label. Authentication failure remains an actionable readiness error.

Tradeoff: a custom or unreported override could escape detection and incur charges without a separate Kiln approval. This safeguards detected overrides; it does not certify that every allowed run uses subscription billing. Detection must still be implemented and validated, with diagnostic failures visible.

Choose Change if missing details should instead require one explicit confirmation of the existing Claude Code settings, or describe a different behavior.

Why this is proposed

Doug rejected the alarming “billing unknown / needs attention” presentation and asked to reconsider its behavior, but did not settle every incomplete-metadata case. Existing account handling accepts successful sign-in without a plan name. Local and documented authentication behavior does not establish how often other installations omit billing details. Blocking or asking for confirmation whenever metadata is incomplete would add the friction Doug challenged.

02 / SECTION

Make API billing a deliberate choice

A detected separately billed route needs an explicit choice. The decision beside these screens defines how long that choice lasts.

Key acceptance criteria & mockups

  • An initially unticked choice identifies direct API billing or the configured provider and its source without exposing credentials. The choice applies to the billing information reviewed; changed information cannot inherit an old click. AC-BILL-04
  • The user can change the detected source and recheck instead of approving. Kiln does not remove credentials or rewrite provider settings; rechecking starts no AI work. AC-BILL-06
  • Every AI launch or resume checks the current billing context. An unapproved detected route holds the next launch at Needs you and preserves the recorded session and completed work. Approving alone does not resume it. AC-RUN-01–03
  • These are launch-time checks, not a spending cap or per-request protection. Settings changed during a running session do not automatically interrupt it. Local completion checks remain available; any resulting AI work must pass the billing check. AC-RUN-04
  • Running views retain the billing facts recorded at launch. New facts are labelled for the next run; disconnected views are last known and offer no actionable approval or launch controls. AC-RUN-05

What should work or look differently in this section?

Assumptions to confirm

BILLING-001Confidence: 90%Controls when separately billed work can continue without another approval.Unanswered

Should API approval last for the current PRD's entire execution?

One explicit approval covers the current PRD execution, including later phases and restarts, while its confirmed billing context stays the same.

A different billing context requires fresh approval; a different PRD or a new execution after completion cannot reuse it. The user can clear approval while no AI session is running.

A different provider, credential source, known payer identity, or detectably changed credential requires new approval. Switching away from that metered context invalidates its approval.

Choose Change if approval should instead be required after every Kiln restart, or describe a different scope or duration.

Why this is proposed

Doug distinguished an accidental API override from paid overflow deliberately enabled in Claude, but did not specify API-approval duration. Existing recovery carries one PRD through usage waits and application restarts. Approval on every process start would repeatedly interrupt that flow; indefinite approval across unrelated PRDs would be broader than the choice shown. For example, approval for a usage-limit recovery PRD would survive a restart in that execution but would not approve this separate billing-safeguards PRD; this is illustrative, not a real paid run.

03 / SECTION

Show Codex credits without changing eligibility

Codex keeps ChatGPT sign-in and the OpenAI provider as its eligibility rules. There are no open assumptions to answer in this section; comments on its requirements and screens are welcome.

Key acceptance criteria & mockups

  • The ChatGPT account summary shows its email, reported plan when available, and a link to ChatGPT usage settings. Unavailable account or plan details are labelled unavailable; no included-only or zero-extra-cost promise is made. AC-CODEX-01
  • Reported credits appear as a factual balance or availability statement for the same account or workspace, with workspace-wide scope clearly identified. There is no acknowledgement checkbox. Missing, stale or unattributable credit data adds no warning or invented zero balance. AC-CODEX-02
  • A credit balance does not prove paid usage or auto-reload is enabled, that the run is spending credits, or that automatic recovery is permitted. Existing usage and recovery rules still decide continuation; Kiln never purchases credits or changes spending settings. AC-CODEX-02, AC-CODEX-04
  • API-key-only authentication still requires ChatGPT sign-in with codex login; another provider still requires changing Codex settings to OpenAI. Claude API approval cannot bypass either restriction or other readiness checks. AC-CODEX-03
  • All reported usage windows remain. Billing and credits follow the selected account before Start and the recorded account during a run; switching agents cannot leave another account’s data visible as current. AC-CODEX-04–05
